rows.subtype: Approach: first-principles reading of the core concept [Thinking]
rows.description: Before jumping into a framework, a student learns what problem it solves and its main building blocks, so later tutorials fit into a clear map.

rows.subtype: Approach: building a small project immediately [Action]
rows.description: The student follows a short tutorial for one day, then builds a simple expense tracker with the new tool, and learns more from errors than from videos.

rows.subtype: Approach: tutorial hell without building [Pitfall]
rows.description: The student watches course after course, nodding along, but cannot write anything from a blank file, since watching felt like learning but built no skill.

rows.subtype: Approach: teaching back to check understanding [Revision]
rows.description: The student explains the concept to a junior and discovers gaps at the second question, then goes back to fix that piece before moving on.

rows.subtopic: An unrealistic deadline from a manager
rows.subtype: Approach: breaking work into estimated pieces to test feasibility [Thinking]
rows.description: Told to deliver a payments feature in two weeks, a developer lists every task with hours and sees it needs six weeks. The numbers give her a factual base rather than a feeling.

rows.subtopic: An unrealistic deadline from a manager
rows.subtype: Approach: offering scope options instead of a flat no [Action]
rows.description: She brings the manager three choices: full feature in six weeks, core flow in two weeks with manual reconciliation, or a two-week prototype. The manager picks the core flow.

rows.subtopic: An unrealistic deadline from a manager
rows.subtype: Approach: accepting silently and working nights [Pitfall]
rows.description: A junior lead says yes without checking the estimate and starts working until midnight. Quality falls, bugs reach production, and the manager assumes the deadline was reasonable next time.

rows.subtopic: An unrealistic deadline from a manager
rows.subtype: Approach: early risk flag with updated forecast [Revision]
rows.description: Midway, a vendor delay appears. She tells the manager the same day, shares a revised date, and suggests one task be moved to another team, avoiding a last-minute surprise.

rows.subtype: Approach: working backward from exam dates and syllabus weight [Thinking]
rows.description: A Class 10 student counts backward from the March exam date, lists chapters by marks weightage, and sees that Science and Maths need the most hours, so those get the early mornings.

rows.subtype: Approach: task decomposition into chapter-level checklists [Action]
rows.description: The student turns each subject into a tick-box list of chapters, past-paper sets and formula sheets, and ticks items off nightly, which makes progress visible instead of a vague feeling of being behind.

rows.subtype: Approach: copying a topper's timetable without fit [Pitfall]
rows.description: A student adopts a classmate's 5 am to midnight routine from social media. It ignores her own energy pattern and school hours, so by week two she is exhausted and abandons the whole schedule.

rows.subtype: Approach: buffer and slack planning [Revision]
rows.description: After missing two days to fever, the student sees the plan had no gaps. She rebuilds it with one free half-day per week and moves the missed chapters there instead of piling them on top.

rows.subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
rows.subtype: Approach: establishing the facts before acting [Thinking]
rows.description: On noticing inflated numbers in a client report, an analyst re-checks the calculations and sources and separates what is known from what is suspected before accusing anyone.

rows.subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
rows.subtype: Approach: consulting a mentor outside the company [Action]
rows.description: The employee talks in general terms to a trusted mentor in another firm to test judgement and understand how others handled similar situations, without leaking confidential details.

rows.subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
rows.subtype: Approach: staying silent to protect the job [Pitfall]
rows.description: Fearing for a loan-backed salary, the employee says nothing and tells themselves it is not their business. Later the problem grows and the employee's silence weighs on their conscience.

rows.subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
rows.subtype: Approach: escalating to compliance if unresolved [Revision]
rows.description: When the manager dismisses the issue, the employee sends a written note to the compliance team or ethics helpline, following official process and avoiding gossip or social media.

rows.subtype: Approach: making a guest list with a limit on numbers [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy wants to invite his whole class but his parents can host fifteen. He lists close friends and cousins first, counts, and cuts a few, choosing who matters most.

rows.subtype: Approach: dreaming up ideas and then choosing one [Thinking]
rows.description: A girl brainstorms a treasure hunt, a movie and a pizza party, then compares them for cost, space and fun. She picks the treasure hunt because it works in their small flat.

rows.subtype: Approach: planning only the fun parts and ignoring food and time [Pitfall]
rows.description: A girl plans five games but forgets snacks and how long each takes. On the day, kids get hungry at 5 pm and the games run beyond the time when parents come to pick them up.

rows.subtype: Approach: checking the budget with a parent and trimming [Revision]
rows.description: The costs of balloons, return gifts and cake exceed what a parent set aside. The child cuts return gifts to small pencil sets and makes decorations from coloured paper at home.

rows.subtype: Approach: simple step list [Action]
rows.description: A child follows a picture list taped inside the cupboard: water bottle, lunch box, notebook, pencil box. Each item is put in and ticked.

rows.subtype: Approach: asking an adult [Action]
rows.description: A child asks mother, "What do I need for tomorrow?" and she reads the timetable aloud. The child then puts in the books she names.

rows.subtype: Approach: not checking [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child throws items in quickly and later finds the lunch box left on the table. Packing felt finished without any check against the list.

rows.subtype: Approach: make-believe rehearsal [Revision]
rows.description: After forgetting the water bottle, a child pretends to walk through the school day, saying "Now I am thirsty, I need my bottle." The rehearsal shows what is missing.
